title: Testing, Debugging, and Deployment
summary: Prove your code works, find out why it doesn't, and ship it safely to production.

lessons.title: Test Data That Never Lies
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine how to test Apex classes and triggers, including the use of mocks and stubs (HttpCalloutMock, Stub API, Test.startTest/stopTest, test data).

cards.title: Empty org by default
cards.body: Since API **24.0**, tests **can't see org data**. Every test starts with an empty database (except setup-ish objects like **User, Profile, RecordType, Organization**). You build the data you need.

cards.title: Test data factory
cards.body: One place to build records. A new required field? Fix it once, every test is green again.

cards.title: @TestSetup
cards.body: Runs **once per class**. Each test method gets a **fresh copy**: changes in one method are rolled back before the next.

cards.title: Data from a CSV
cards.body: **Test.loadData** reads a CSV **static resource** and inserts the rows. Good when admins own the sample data.
**SeeAllData=true** makes tests depend on whatever is in the org, so they break between sandboxes. Also: **@TestSetup is not supported** in a class annotated @isTest(SeeAllData=true).
SOSL returns **nothing** in tests until you call **Test.setFixedSearchResults(ids)**. Think: "SOSL is shy in tests - give it a script."

lessons.title: startTest, stopTest, Async Magic
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine how to test Apex classes and triggers, including the use of mocks and stubs (HttpCalloutMock, Stub API, Test.startTest/stopTest, test data).

cards.title: Test.startTest() / stopTest() do 2 things
items: Code between them gets a **fresh set of governor limits**
Async work queued between them (future, queueable, batch, scheduled) **runs synchronously at stopTest()**
Only **one** startTest/stopTest pair per test method

cards.title: Testing Batch Apex
cards.body: Assert **after** stopTest. A test can only run **one execute()** chunk, so keep records within the scope size.

cards.title: Scheduled Apex
cards.body: Call **System.schedule** between start/stop. The job's execute() runs at **stopTest()**, no matter what the cron says. You can also query **CronTrigger** to check the cron expression and next fire time.

cards.title: Platform events
cards.body: Events published in a test are held in a **test event bus** until stopTest() or **Test.getEventBus().deliver()**.
Queueable **chaining isn't allowed in tests** (enqueueing a job from a queueable throws an error). Docs suggest guarding the chain call with **Test.isRunningTest()**.
"**Stop** means **Go**": async code doesn't run until you hit **stopTest()**. Assertions before it see the world before the job ran.

lessons.title: Run As, Assert, Don't Cheat
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine how to test Apex classes and triggers, including the use of mocks and stubs (HttpCalloutMock, Stub API, Test.startTest/stopTest, test data).

cards.title: System.runAs(user)
cards.body: Runs a block as another user. It enforces **record sharing** only. It does **not** enforce **object or field permissions** for code running in system mode.

runAs = "**R**ecords, not **R**ights". To test permissions, the code itself must check them (e.g., **WITH USER_MODE**, **AccessLevel.USER_MODE**, stripInaccessible) - then runAs makes those checks use the test user.

cards.title: Mixed DML fix
cards.body: Inserting a **User** (setup object) and an **Account** in one test throws **MIXED_DML_OPERATION**. Wrap the setup-object DML in **System.runAs()**, or move it to an **@future** method.

cards.title: Assert class + expected exceptions
cards.body: **Assert.fail** guarantees the test fails if no exception is thrown. Also: areEqual(expected, actual), isNull, isInstanceOfType.
**if (Test.isRunningTest())** branches mean tests run **different code than production**. Coverage looks fine, real bugs hide. Prefer mocks and dependency injection.

lessons.title: Fake the Internet: Callout Mocks
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine how to test Apex classes and triggers, including the use of mocks and stubs (HttpCalloutMock, Stub API, Test.startTest/stopTest, test data).

cards.title: No real callouts in tests
cards.body: Test methods **can't make real callouts**. Without a mock, the test fails. You register a fake with **Test.setMock()**.

cards.title: HttpCalloutMock
cards.body: One method: **respond(HttpRequest)** returns an **HttpResponse**.

cards.title: Many endpoints, static resources
cards.body: One endpoint? Use **StaticResourceCalloutMock**. Several? **MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock**.

cards.title: SOAP (WSDL2Apex)
cards.body: SOAP mocks put the fake response into the map under **response_x**.
"**You have uncommitted work pending**": do your test **DML before Test.startTest()**, then make the callout **inside** startTest/stopTest.

lessons.title: Stub API: Mock Your Own Classes
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine how to test Apex classes and triggers, including the use of mocks and stubs (HttpCalloutMock, Stub API, Test.startTest/stopTest, test data).

cards.title: Why stub?
cards.body: Unit test class A without running real class B (slow queries, callouts, complex setup). The **Stub API** builds a fake B at runtime.

cards.title: StubProvider
cards.body: Every call on the stub lands in **handleMethodCall**. You decide the return value by method name/args.

cards.title: Create and inject
cards.body: **Test.createStub(Type, StubProvider)** returns an Object - cast it. Then inject it into the class under test.

cards.title: Can't be stubbed
items: Batchable classes, classes with only private constructors

cards.body: Stub API needs a **seam**: the class under test must accept the dependency (constructor/setter). No injection point = nothing to swap.

lessons.title: Testing LWC (Jest) and VF Controllers
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, identify how to test and debug Lightning web components, Aura components, Visualforce, and JavaScript (including Jest unit tests for LWC).

cards.title: Jest = local unit tests
cards.body: LWC tests run in **Node.js with Jest** via **@salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest**. No org, no browser. Files live in a **__tests__** folder as ***.test.js**. They **don't count** toward Apex coverage.

cards.title: Mock a wire adapter
cards.body: Wire adapters are test adapters: **.emit(data)** pushes data, **.error()** pushes an error.

cards.title: Mock imperative Apex
cards.body: **virtual: true** because the Apex module doesn't exist on disk.
DOM updates are **async**. After setting a property or emitting data, **await Promise.resolve()** (or a flushPromises helper) before asserting.

cards.title: Visualforce extension test
cards.body: Set the page and URL params, build the **StandardController**, then call action methods and check **ApexPages.getMessages()**.

lessons.title: Debug Like a Detective
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine why Apex code is not behaving as expected and how to debug it (debug logs, checkpoints, Apex Replay Debugger).

cards.body: "**Every Wise Investigator Digs For Finer Facts**" = Error, Warn, Info, Debug, Fine, Finer, Finest. A System.debug at level X shows only if the **Apex Code** category is X or louder.

cards.title: Trace flags
cards.body: A **trace flag** = who/what to log + a **debug level** + a time window (max **24 hours**). Set on a **user**, **Apex class/trigger**, or Automated Process. **Class/trigger flags override** the levels for that code - great for muting a chatty class.

cards.title: Apex Replay Debugger
cards.body: Free, in **VS Code**. Capture a debug log (Apex Code **FINEST**), then "replay" it: **breakpoints**, variables, call stack. Add **checkpoints** to capture heap dumps. Works on any org, even production, because it only reads logs.

cards.title: Developer Console
cards.body: Logs, **checkpoints** (up to **5**, heap snapshot at a line, no code changes), Query Editor, **Execution Overview** / Timeline for slow spots.

cards.title: Limits class
cards.code:
System.debug(Limits.getQueries() + ' of ' + Limits.getLimitQueries() + ' SOQL used');
System.debug('CPU ms: ' + Limits.getCpuTime());
cards.body: getX() = used so far; getLimitX() = the max.
Unhandled exception emails go to the **last developer who modified** the class/trigger, plus anyone added in Setup > **Apex Exception Email**.

lessons.title: Orgs, CLI, Packages, Change Sets
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, formulate the deployment process, supporting tools, and mechanisms for source-driven development (Salesforce CLI, scratch orgs, packages, metadata/destructive changes).

cards.title: Sandbox cheat sheet
items: **Developer**: metadata only, no prod data (200 MB), refresh daily
**Developer Pro**: metadata only, more storage (1 GB), refresh daily
**Partial Copy**: metadata + sample data via **sandbox template**, refresh every **5 days**
**Full**: complete copy, refresh every **29 days** - perf/UAT/staging

cards.title: Scratch org loop (sf CLI)
cards.code:
sf org create scratch --definition-file config/project-scratch-def.json \
  --alias feature1 --duration-days 7 --target-dev-hub DevHub
sf project deploy start --target-org feature1
sf project retrieve start --target-org feature1
cards.body: Scratch orgs: disposable (1-30 days), built from source, **source tracking** on. Created from a **Dev Hub**.

cards.title: Packages
cards.body: **Unlocked packages** (2GP) = versioned, upgradeable bundles of your metadata built from source with a Dev Hub. To **promote** a version to released, it needs **75% Apex code coverage** (create it with **--code-coverage**).

**Change sets**: only between orgs tied to the **same production org**, need a **deployment connection**, and **can't delete** components. To delete, use **destructiveChanges.xml** with the Metadata API / CLI.

cards.title: Deleting metadata
cards.body: destructiveChanges(Pre/Post).xml + a package.xml. CLI: **--pre-destructive-changes / --post-destructive-changes**.
**DevOps Center** = click-based, Git-backed pipeline (work items, stages) - the modern replacement for change sets.

lessons.title: Test Levels, Coverage, Quick Deploy
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, formulate the deployment process, supporting tools, and mechanisms for source-driven development (Salesforce CLI, scratch orgs, packages, metadata/destructive changes).

cards.title: Production deploy rules
items: Test classes and System.debug lines don't count toward coverage

cards.title: Test levels
items: **NoTestRun** - default for non-production (not allowed in prod for Apex)
**RunSpecifiedTests** - only listed tests; **each** class/trigger deployed needs **75%** from them
**RunLocalTests** - all except managed-package tests; prod default when deploying Apex

cards.title: Validate now, deploy later
cards.code:
sf project deploy validate --source-dir force-app \
  --test-level RunLocalTests --target-org prod
sf project deploy quick --job-id 0AfXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX --target-org prod
cards.body: **Quick deploy** skips re-running tests if validation passed within the last **10 days**.
RunSpecifiedTests checks coverage **per component**, not org-wide. 85% org-wide does not save a class sitting at 60%.

cards.title: Flows too
cards.body: If "**Deploy processes and flows as active**" is on, production needs enough flow test coverage (75% of active autolaunched flows/processes) from tests that fire them.

questions.q: A new test method queries Accounts and gets zero rows, even though the sandbox has thousands of Accounts. The class has a plain @isTest annotation. What explains this?
options: Sharing rules hide the Accounts, because test methods run as an automated user with no record access
By default, tests can't see existing org data; they must create their own
SOQL is blocked in test methods unless wrapped in Test.startTest()
The query must use ALL ROWS to see records in tests
questions.explain: Since API 24.0, test methods are isolated from org data unless SeeAllData=true. Tests should create their own data.
wrong: Tests run as the user who started them, in system mode. The issue is data isolation, not sharing.
SOQL works anywhere in a test method.
ALL ROWS returns deleted/archived rows; it doesn't reveal org data to tests.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Isolation of Test Data from Organization Data

questions.q: A test class has an @TestSetup method that inserts an Account with Rating = 'Warm'. Test method A updates it to 'Hot'. Test method B then queries the Account and checks Rating. What does B see?
options: 'Hot', because @TestSetup data is shared and committed across methods
An error, because the record was modified by another method
'Warm', because each method gets its own copy of the setup data
It depends on the method execution order, which is alphabetical
questions.explain: Records from @TestSetup are rolled back after each test method, so every method starts with the original values.
wrong: Changes in one method are rolled back before the next.
No locking error happens; each method is isolated.
Results don't depend on order because each method gets a clean copy.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Using Test Setup Methods

questions.q: A test runs without SeeAllData. Which two kinds of existing records can it query without creating them first? (Choose 2)
options: Profile records
Existing Account records
Custom setting records
RecordType records
Existing Case records
questions.explain: Setup-type objects such as User, Profile, RecordType and Organization are visible to tests without SeeAllData. Business data and custom setting data are not.
wrong: Business data like Accounts is hidden from tests by default.
Custom setting data must be inserted by the test.
Cases are org data and are hidden by default.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Isolation of Test Data from Organization Data

questions.q: An admin maintains a spreadsheet of 30 realistic Accounts that several test classes should use. The developer wants tests to stay independent of org data. What is the best approach?
options: Load the data with Data Loader and use @isTest(SeeAllData=true)
Query the CSV from a Document record inside @TestSetup
Hard-code the Account IDs from the sandbox in the tests
Upload the CSV as a static resource and call Test.loadData
questions.explain: Test.loadData inserts rows from a CSV static resource inside the test, so the data stays isolated and is easy for admins to update.
wrong: SeeAllData ties tests to org contents that differ between environments.
Documents are org data and aren't visible to tests without SeeAllData.
IDs differ between orgs and the records won't be visible.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Loading Test Data

questions.q: A method under test runs a SOSL search. In the test, the search always returns no results even though the test inserted matching Contacts. What should the developer do?
options: Call Test.setFixedSearchResults with the IDs the search should return
Add SeeAllData=true so SOSL can use the search index
Call Test.stopTest() before the search so the inserted Contacts get added to the search index
Replace the SOSL in production code with a SOQL LIKE query
questions.explain: SOSL in test context returns empty results unless Test.setFixedSearchResults defines the records to return.
wrong: SeeAllData doesn't make SOSL return the test's own records.
stopTest runs async jobs; it doesn't index records.
Changing production code to fit a test is the wrong fix.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Adding SOSL Queries to Unit Tests

questions.q: What are two effects of wrapping code in Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest()? (Choose 2)
options: The code between them gets a fresh set of governor limits
Records inserted between them are committed to the org
Asynchronous work queued between them runs when stopTest() is called
Validation rules are skipped between them
Callouts made between them are allowed without registering a mock with Test.setMock
questions.explain: startTest/stopTest give the enclosed code its own limits and force queued async Apex to finish at stopTest.
wrong: Test data is never committed.
Validation rules still run.
Callouts still need Test.setMock.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Using Limits, startTest, and stopTest

questions.q: A test calls Database.executeBatch between Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest(), but its Assert statements are placed right after executeBatch and before stopTest. The assertions fail. What is the fix?
options: Increase the batch scope to 2000
Move the assertions after Test.stopTest()
Call the batch's execute() method twice
Add SeeAllData=true so the job can see its records
questions.explain: The batch only runs when stopTest() is called, so assertions must come after it.
wrong: Scope size doesn't change when the job runs.
Calling execute manually isn't needed and skips start/finish.
The job sees the test's own records already.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Batch Apex

questions.q: An Apex trigger subscribes to Order_Event__e and creates a Task. A test publishes the event with EventBus.publish and immediately queries Tasks, finding none. What should the developer add before the query?
options: A call to System.enqueueJob for the trigger
SeeAllData=true on the test class
A loop that re-queries Tasks until one appears or the CPU time limit is close
Test.getEventBus().deliver() or Test.stopTest()
questions.explain: In tests, published events are held on a test event bus until Test.stopTest() or Test.getEventBus().deliver() delivers them to subscribers.
wrong: Event triggers aren't queueables.
Data visibility isn't the issue.
Apex has no sleep, and polling never delivers the event; delivery must be forced.
questions.source: Platform Events Developer Guide: Testing Your Platform Event in Apex

questions.q: A Schedulable class is scheduled in a test with a cron expression for next January. The test calls System.schedule between Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest(). What happens to the job in the test?
options: It never runs; the test must call execute() directly to cover it
The test waits until the cron time and then times out
Its execute() runs at Test.stopTest(), so its effects can be asserted afterwards
It runs only if the test class has SeeAllData=true
questions.explain: Async work scheduled after startTest runs synchronously at stopTest, including scheduled jobs, regardless of the cron time. CronTrigger can also be queried to check the schedule.
wrong: The job does run at stopTest.
Tests don't wait for real time.
Scheduling doesn't depend on SeeAllData.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing the Apex Scheduler

questions.q: A Queueable job re-enqueues itself to process the next chunk of records. Its test fails with an error when the job tries to chain. What is the documented way to keep the job testable?
options: Guard the chaining call with Test.isRunningTest() and test one link of the chain
Call Test.stopTest() twice to run each chained job
Mark the test with @isTest(SeeAllData=true)
Convert the chain to a for loop inside one execute() call
questions.explain: Older Apex versions threw an error when a test tried to chain queueable jobs, so the Queueable docs suggested checking Test.isRunningTest() before chaining and testing one link. Current docs also allow testing chains with a suitable maximum stack depth (AsyncOptions).
wrong: Only one startTest/stopTest pair is allowed per test method.
SeeAllData doesn't affect queueable chaining.
That defeats the reason for chaining (fresh limits per job).
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Queueable Apex

questions.q: A class saved at API version 66.0 is tested to prove that a user without access to the Salary__c field can't read it. Inside System.runAs(limitedUser), a SOQL query in a "with sharing" class returns Salary__c values. Why?
options: runAs only applies to users inserted in @TestSetup, so a user inserted in the test method is ignored
runAs enforces record sharing, not field-level security; the query needs user mode (WITH USER_MODE)
Field-level security is never enforced in tests
The class must be declared inherited sharing, because with sharing ignores the runAs user's access
questions.explain: At API 66.0, Apex runs in system mode by default and runAs only adds the user's record sharing. To have FLS checked, the code must enforce it, for example with WITH USER_MODE or stripInaccessible.
wrong: runAs works with any user, inserted or not.
FLS is enforced in tests when the code enforces it, such as user mode queries.
Sharing keywords control record access, not FLS, and with sharing already respects the runAs user.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the runAs Method

questions.q: A test inserts a User with a specific Profile and UserRole, then inserts an Account owned by that User, and fails with MIXED_DML_OPERATION. Which two changes fix it? (Choose 2)
options: Wrap the User insert in a System.runAs() block
Insert the User and Account in a single List<SObject>
Use Database.insert with allOrNone set to false
Insert the User from an @future method called inside Test.startTest()/stopTest()
Add SeeAllData=true to the test class
questions.explain: Setup and non-setup DML can't mix in one transaction. In tests, putting the setup DML in a runAs block or in a future method separates them.
wrong: Mixing types in one list still mixes setup and non-setup DML.
Partial success doesn't change the mixed DML rule.
Data visibility doesn't affect mixed DML.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Setup and Non-Setup Objects in DML

questions.q: A test must prove that OrderService.submit(null) throws OrderService.OrderException. Which pattern makes the test fail if no exception is thrown?
options: Call the method and then Assert.isNull(result)
Wrap the call in try/catch and assert on the exception in catch, with nothing after the call in try
Use Assert.areEqual(OrderException.class, OrderService.submit(null))
Call it in try, then Assert.fail(); in the catch block, assert on the exception
questions.explain: Assert.fail() right after the call only runs when no exception happens, so the test fails as it should. The catch block then checks the exception.
wrong: If an exception is thrown, the assert never runs, and the check proves nothing.
If no exception is thrown, the catch block never runs and nothing fails, so the test still passes.
This doesn't compile into a meaningful exception check.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Assert Class

questions.q: A class contains: if (Test.isRunningTest()) { return fakeRate; } else { return callRateApi(); }. Tests pass with 90% coverage, but production keeps failing. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: The real callout path never runs in tests, so its defects stay hidden
Test.isRunningTest() throws an exception in production orgs
This is the recommended pattern for avoiding callouts in tests
Replacing the branch with an HttpCalloutMock registered via Test.setMock lets tests run the real code path
Branches that use Test.isRunningTest() are excluded from coverage calculations
questions.explain: Test-only branches make tests run different code than production. A callout mock lets the real code run in tests with a fake response.
wrong: It just returns false in production.
Docs recommend mocks for callouts, not test-only branches.
Those lines are counted like any other code.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts

questions.q: Which method must a class implement to act as an HttpCalloutMock?
options: HttpResponse respond(HttpRequest req)
void doInvoke(Object stub, Object request, Map<String, Object> response, ...)
Object handleMethodCall(Object stubbedObject, String stubbedMethodName, ...)
HttpRequest send(HttpResponse res)
questions.explain: HttpCalloutMock has a single method that takes the request and returns a fake HttpResponse.
wrong: doInvoke belongs to WebServiceMock (SOAP).
handleMethodCall belongs to StubProvider.
No such method; the signature is reversed.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts by Implementing the HttpCalloutMock Interface

questions.q: A test inserts an Account and then calls a method that makes an HTTP callout. Test.setMock is set, but the test fails with "You have uncommitted work pending". What should the developer change?
options: Use SeeAllData=true so no DML is needed
Replace the HttpCalloutMock with a WebServiceMock, which allows DML before a callout in one transaction
Do the DML before Test.startTest() and make the callout between startTest() and stopTest()
Make the callout from a trigger on Account
questions.explain: Putting the DML before startTest and the callout inside the startTest/stopTest block avoids the uncommitted-work error in tests.
wrong: Relying on org data breaks isolation and isn't the fix.
WebServiceMock is for SOAP callouts and doesn't lift the uncommitted work rule.
Triggers can't make synchronous callouts.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Performing DML Operations and Mock Callouts

questions.q: A method calls a rates endpoint and a fees endpoint in the same transaction. The team keeps sample JSON for each in separate static resources. Which mock fits best?
options: StaticResourceCalloutMock
MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock
WebServiceMock
A StubProvider for the Http class
questions.explain: MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock maps each endpoint to its own static resource, so one mock covers both callouts.
wrong: It returns the same single resource for every callout.
WebServiceMock is for SOAP callouts from WSDL2Apex classes.
System types like Http can't be stubbed.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts Using MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock

questions.q: A developer used WSDL2Apex to generate a SOAP client. How should the test supply a fake response?
options: Implement HttpCalloutMock and return the SOAP envelope XML as the response body from respond()
Use Test.createStub on the generated port class
Set the endpoint to a Remote Site of localhost
Implement WebServiceMock and put the response element into the map with key 'response_x'
questions.explain: SOAP callouts made through WSDL2Apex classes are mocked with WebServiceMock and Test.setMock(WebServiceMock.class, ...).
wrong: HttpCalloutMock covers HTTP callouts made with the Http class, not WSDL2Apex SOAP callouts.
The Stub API isn't the documented approach for WSDL2Apex callouts.
Tests can't make real callouts at all.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Test Web Service Callouts

questions.q: A WeatherMock class implementing HttpCalloutMock exists in the org. The test below fails. What is the most likely cause?
options: Callout tests require @isTest(SeeAllData=true)
Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new WeatherMock()) is never called, so a real callout is tried
A Remote Site Setting for the endpoint is missing
Assert.areEqual has expected and actual in the wrong order, which makes it fail even on equal values

wrong: Callout mocks don't need org data.

Argument order affects the failure message, not the result.

questions.q: A developer wants to use the Stub API to replace a dependency in a unit test. Which member of the dependency class can be stubbed?

A private instance method
A public instance method
A property getter
questions.explain: The Stub API can intercept public (and protected/global) instance methods. Static methods, private methods and properties can't be stubbed.
wrong: Static methods can't be stubbed.
Private methods can't be stubbed.
Properties (getters/setters) can't be stubbed.

questions.q: How does a test create a stubbed instance of the PricingService class using a StubProvider named PricingStub?
options: (PricingService) Test.createStub(PricingService.class, new PricingStub())
Test.setMock(PricingService.class, new PricingStub())
new PricingService(new PricingStub())
PricingStub.createStub(PricingService.class)

wrong: Test.setMock is for callout mocks only.
That just calls a real constructor.

questions.q: Given the stub provider and test code below, what are the values of d and label?
options: d = 0.25 and label = 'GOLD'
Both are null; stubs need an explicit when() setup
A runtime error, because the provider must return a non-null value for every method
d = 0.25 and label = null
questions.explain: Every call on the stub goes to handleMethodCall. getDiscount matches and returns 0.25; getTierLabel falls through to return null. The real methods never run.
wrong: The real getTierLabel never runs, so nothing returns 'GOLD'.

Returning null is allowed.

questions.q: Where do Lightning Web Component Jest tests run?

In the browser via the Lightning Testing Service only
Locally in Node.js using @salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest, with no org needed
In a scratch org, during sf project deploy start
