wrong: Jest tests are separate from Apex tests.
Jest runs in Node with jsdom, not in an org browser session.
Deployments run Apex tests, not Jest.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Test Lightning Web Components

questions.q: The Jest test below fails: the paragraph still shows the old greeting. What should the developer change?
options: Use document.querySelector instead of shadowRoot.querySelector
Make the test async and await Promise.resolve() after setting el.name, then query
Set el.name before calling createElement
Call el.connectedCallback() manually after setting the property, so the template renders again
questions.explain: LWC re-renders asynchronously. Awaiting a resolved promise lets the re-render finish before the assertion.
wrong: Component content lives in the shadow tree.
Properties are set on the created element, not before it exists.
The engine calls lifecycle hooks; the problem is timing.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Write Jest Tests for Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A component uses @wire(getRecord, ...) from lightning/uiRecordApi. How should a Jest test supply record data to the component?
options: Import getRecord in the test and call getRecord.emit(mockData)
Call Test.setMock(getRecord, mockData)
Assign the data to el.record directly from the test
Deploy sample records to a scratch org and run the test with --target-org so the wire gets data
questions.explain: sfdx-lwc-jest supplies test wire adapters. Calling emit() on the imported adapter pushes mock data into the component's wired property or function.
wrong: Test.setMock is an Apex method.
Wired properties are private to the component and not settable from outside.
Jest tests don't use org data.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Test Wire Service

questions.q: A component calls the Apex method AccountController.getAccounts imperatively. Which two steps let a Jest test control its result? (Choose 2)
options: Deploy the Apex class and run the Jest test against the org
Call Test.setMock inside the Jest test file
Use jest.mock on '@salesforce/apex/AccountController.getAccounts' with { virtual: true }, returning { default: jest.fn() }
Register the method as a wire adapter with createLdsTestWireAdapter, then call emit() with the mock data
Use mockResolvedValue or mockRejectedValue on the mocked function to simulate success or an error
questions.explain: Apex imports are mocked as virtual modules whose default export is a jest.fn(); the test then sets its resolved or rejected value.
wrong: Jest tests don't call real Apex.
Test.setMock is Apex, not JavaScript.
Imperative calls aren't wire adapters, and that helper is deprecated.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Mock Apex Methods in Jest Tests

questions.q: A Visualforce page uses an extension of the Account standard controller and reads the id URL parameter. How should the test set up the controller?
options: Construct the extension with a null StandardController and pass the record id in a public static variable
Use SeeAllData=true, load the page with PageReference.getContent(), then read the extension from it
Call the extension's constructor from an @future method
Call Test.setCurrentPage, add the id to its parameters, then pass new ApexPages.StandardController(acc)
questions.explain: Test.setCurrentPage plus page parameters recreate the request context, and a StandardController wraps the test record for the extension.
wrong: The extension needs a real StandardController.
getContent can't be used this way for controller testing, and tests should create their own data.
Async context is not needed.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Testing Custom Controllers and Controller Extensions

questions.q: The Apex Code log category is set to DEBUG. A statement System.debug(LoggingLevel.FINE, msg) does not appear in the log. Why?
options: FINE is more verbose than DEBUG, so Apex Code must be set to FINE, FINER or FINEST
System.debug only logs messages at ERROR level by default
FINE messages are written only while the Apex Replay Debugger is attached, so they never show in normal logs
The Profiling category must be set to FINE
questions.explain: A debug statement appears only when the category level is at least as verbose as the statement level. FINE sits below DEBUG in the order.
wrong: Without a level argument, System.debug uses DEBUG.
Replay Debugger reads logs that already exist; it doesn't change what gets written.
Apex Code controls System.debug output.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Debug Log Levels

questions.q: Debug logs for a transaction hit the size limit because a utility class writes thousands of FINEST lines. The developer still needs full detail from OrderService. What should they do?
options: Delete the System.debug statements from the utility class in production
Set the user trace flag to NONE for all categories, so the log only keeps the OrderService output
Add a class trace flag on the utility class with a debug level that sets Apex Code to ERROR
Enable Event Monitoring for Apex execution
questions.explain: Class and trigger trace flags override the log levels for that code, so the noisy class can be muted while the user's trace flag keeps full detail elsewhere.
wrong: Editing production code just to fix logging is risky and unnecessary.
That would hide OrderService output too.
Event Monitoring doesn't control debug log verbosity.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Set Up Debug Logging (Trace Flags)

questions.q: A bug only happens in production. The org has no Apex Interactive Debugger sessions. The developer wants to step through the code and inspect variable values. What should they use?
options: Developer Console Query Editor
Apex Replay Debugger in VS Code, using a debug log captured with Apex Code at FINEST
Test.startTest() in Anonymous Apex
Deploy extra System.debug statements with a change set, then step through them in the Developer Console
questions.explain: The Apex Replay Debugger replays a captured debug log, offering breakpoints, variables and call stacks without a live debugging session.
wrong: The Query Editor runs SOQL; it doesn't step through code.
startTest is only for test methods.
This changes production code, and the Developer Console can't step through code line by line.
questions.source: Salesforce Extensions for VS Code: Apex Replay Debugger

questions.q: A developer needs to see the heap contents and variable values at a specific line in a deployed class without changing its code. Which two options work? (Choose 2)
options: Set a checkpoint on the line in the Developer Console, run the code, and inspect it in the Checkpoints tab
Add System.debug statements for each variable, deploy them to production, and read the values in the log
Use the Apex Replay Debugger with checkpoints and breakpoints on a captured log
Re-run the test with @isTest(SeeAllData=true)
Call Limits.getHeapSize() from Anonymous Apex
questions.explain: Developer Console checkpoints (up to 5) and Replay Debugger checkpoints both capture heap state at a line without code changes.
wrong: That requires a code change and a deployment.
Data visibility doesn't reveal variable state.
It returns a number, not the variable contents at that line.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Set Checkpoints in Apex Code

questions.q: A developer wants code to check, at runtime, how many SOQL queries remain before the limit. Which approach is correct?
options: Read the SOQL count from the debug log header
Call System.getQueryCount()
Use Test.getQueries() in production code
Compare Limits.getQueries() with Limits.getLimitQueries()
questions.explain: Limits.getQueries() returns queries used so far and Limits.getLimitQueries() returns the maximum for the context.
wrong: Code can't read its own debug log.
That method doesn't exist.
That method doesn't exist.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Limits Class

questions.q: An Apex class must be removed from production. The team usually deploys with change sets. What should they use?
options: An outbound change set that excludes the class
A Metadata API deployment with destructiveChanges.xml (e.g. via sf CLI)
Delete the class in Setup in production
Rename the class in a sandbox and deploy it with a change set, which replaces the old class
questions.explain: Change sets can't delete components, and Apex can't be edited directly in production. A destructive changes manifest deployed via the Metadata API removes it.
wrong: Leaving a class out of a change set doesn't delete it.
Production doesn't allow Apex edits or deletes in Setup.
That just adds a second class; the old one stays in production.
questions.source: Metadata API Developer Guide: Deleting Components from an Organization

questions.q: A team wants each developer to work in a short-lived org built from the Git repo, with automatic tracking of local and org changes. What should they use?
options: Scratch orgs created from a Dev Hub
One shared Full sandbox
Change sets between Developer sandboxes
A Partial Copy sandbox per developer
questions.explain: Scratch orgs are disposable, source-driven orgs with source tracking, created from a Dev Hub.
wrong: A shared Full sandbox is slow to refresh and not per-feature.
Change sets don't track source or use Git.
Partial Copy sandboxes are for testing with sample data, refresh only every 5 days, and are a poor fit per feature.
questions.source: Salesforce DX Developer Guide: Scratch Orgs

questions.q: QA needs an environment with all production metadata plus a representative sample of Accounts and Opportunities chosen by a template. It should be refreshable about weekly. Which sandbox fits?
options: Developer
Developer Pro
Partial Copy
Full
questions.explain: Partial Copy sandboxes include metadata plus data selected by a sandbox template and can be refreshed every 5 days.
wrong: Developer sandboxes copy no production data.
Developer Pro also copies no production data.
Full copies all data and only refreshes every 29 days.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Sandbox Types and Templates

questions.q: Which two statements about change sets are true? (Choose 2)
options: They can move metadata between any two Salesforce orgs
The target org must authorize a deployment connection from the source org
They can delete components in the target org
They can't delete components; destructive changes need the Metadata API
They automatically add every dependent component
questions.explain: Change sets only work between orgs linked to the same production org, need a deployment connection, and only add or update components.
wrong: Only orgs affiliated with the same production org.
Deletion isn't supported.
You must add dependencies yourself (there is a "View/Add Dependencies" helper).
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Change Sets

questions.q: A CI job creates an unlocked package version and then runs sf package version promote, which fails. Tests pass locally. What is the most likely cause?
options: Unlocked packages can't contain Apex
The package has no namespace
The Dev Hub must be a sandbox
The version was created without --code-coverage, or its coverage is below 75%
questions.explain: To promote a package version to released, Apex code coverage must be computed during version creation and be at least 75%.
wrong: Unlocked packages can include Apex.
Unlocked packages can be created without a namespace.
A Dev Hub is a production or Developer Edition org, not a sandbox.
questions.source: Salesforce DX Developer Guide: Release an Unlocked Package

questions.q: A deployment to production includes Apex classes, and no test level is specified. Which tests run by default?
options: All local tests (RunLocalTests)
No tests (NoTestRun)
All tests including managed packages (RunAllTestsInOrg)
Only tests named like the deployed classes
questions.explain: For production deployments that contain Apex, the default is to run all local tests, excluding managed-package tests.
wrong: NoTestRun is the default for non-production orgs.
Managed-package tests aren't included by default.
There is no name-matching test level.
questions.source: Metadata API Developer Guide: Running Tests in a Deployment

questions.q: A developer deploys ClassA and ClassB to production with RunSpecifiedTests and two test classes. ClassA reaches 90% coverage, ClassB 60%. Org-wide coverage would be 85%. What happens?
options: It succeeds because org-wide coverage is above 75%
It succeeds because RunSpecifiedTests skips coverage checks
It fails because each deployed class needs 75% coverage from the specified tests
It succeeds, but ClassB is deployed as inactive
questions.explain: With RunSpecifiedTests, every class and trigger in the deployment must individually reach 75% coverage from the tests you list.
wrong: Org-wide coverage isn't the measure for RunSpecifiedTests.
Coverage is still checked, per component.
Apex classes have no inactive state.
questions.source: Metadata API Developer Guide: Running a Subset of Tests in a Deployment

questions.q: A release manager validated a production deployment on Monday and wants to deploy it on Thursday without re-running tests. Which two conditions must be met for quick deploy? (Choose 2)
options: The validation succeeded within the last 10 days
Apex tests passed and the coverage requirements were met during validation
The validation used NoTestRun
The validation targeted a sandbox instead of production
All deployed classes were created by the same user
questions.explain: Quick deploy reuses a successful validation run against the same target org within 10 days in which tests passed and coverage was met.
wrong: Without running tests, there's nothing to reuse for Apex.
The validation must be against the org you deploy to.
Authorship doesn't matter.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Quick Deploy

questions.q: A pricing team's test class creates a Gold tier once in @TestSetup and keeps its Id in a static variable so every test method can reuse it. appliesGoldDiscount fails because the service returns a discount of 0. What is the cause?
options: The Tier__c record is rolled back before appliesGoldDiscount runs, so the tier no longer exists
@TestSetup records can only be read by test methods annotated @IsTest(SeeAllData=true) at method level
goldTierId is null: statics set in @TestSetup reset for each test method. Query the tier instead
Test.startTest() resets all static variables, so goldTierId must be assigned after it
questions.explain: Every test method, including the @TestSetup method, runs in its own transaction, and the static context is set up again each time, so goldTierId is null. The Tier__c record still exists, so the test should query it, for example by Name.
wrong: Setup records stay available to every test method. Only the changes a test method makes are rolled back after that method.
Setup records are visible with default data isolation. @TestSetup isn't even supported in a class with SeeAllData=true.
startTest gives the code a fresh set of governor limits. It doesn't reset variables.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using Test Setup Methods

questions.q: A team is refactoring 30 test classes to share data through @TestSetup methods. During code review, which two statements about test setup methods are correct? (Choose 2)
options: A class annotated @IsTest(SeeAllData=true) at class level can still use @TestSetup to add extra records
If the @TestSetup method throws an exception or an assertion fails, the whole class fails and no test methods run
A class can have one @TestSetup method for each sObject type it seeds
Non-test methods called from the @TestSetup method get no code coverage from that call
Updates that one test method makes to setup records are visible to the test methods that run after it
questions.explain: A fatal error in test setup fails the whole class, and code called from a setup method earns no coverage. Only one @TestSetup method is allowed per class, it isn't supported with SeeAllData=true, and each test method sees the original setup records.
wrong: Test setup methods aren't supported in a class that has access to org data.
Only one test setup method is allowed per test class.
Changes made by a test method are rolled back when that method finishes.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using Test Setup Methods

questions.q: A CPQ developer tests a quote line calculator. The test below throws System.QueryException: List has no rows for assignment to SObject on the marked line, although the sandbox has an active standard price book. What should the developer change?
options: Use Test.getStandardPricebookId() for Pricebook2Id instead of querying the standard price book
Insert a new Pricebook2 with IsStandard = true earlier in the test
Add @IsTest(IsParallel=true) so the test can read shared reference data
Move the query into an @TestSetup method, which can see org data
questions.explain: Without SeeAllData, a test can't query the org's standard price book. Test.getStandardPricebookId() returns its Id anyway, so the test can create standard PricebookEntry records.
wrong: IsStandard can't be set. A test can't create a second standard price book.
IsParallel doesn't open data access, and parallel tests can't even call Test.getStandardPricebookId().
@TestSetup methods have the same data isolation as test methods.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Test Class (getStandardPricebookId)

questions.q: A legacy test class depends on org data. A developer adds a new method and wants only that method isolated from org data. In a sandbox with 5,000 Accounts, what does the query in isolatedCount return?
options: 1, because the method-level SeeAllData=false overrides the class annotation
0, because SeeAllData=false also hides the records the test inserts
It doesn't compile, because a method annotation can't contradict the class annotation
5,001, because SeeAllData=false on a method is ignored when its class has SeeAllData=true
questions.explain: When the class is annotated SeeAllData=true, a method-level SeeAllData=false is ignored, so the method sees every org Account plus the one it inserted. To isolate it, move the method to a class without SeeAllData=true.
wrong: The override only works the other way: a method-level SeeAllData=true overrides a class-level false.
Tests always see the records they create.
It compiles. The method annotation is simply ignored.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the isTest(SeeAllData=True) Annotation

questions.q: To speed up CI runs, a developer marks an invoicing test class as parallel. The test now fails before it reaches its assertion. What is the reason?
options: Queueable jobs started from a test need @IsTest(SeeAllData=true)
Parallel tests (IsParallel=true) can't call System.enqueueJob(). Remove IsParallel or move the test
Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest() aren't allowed in parallel test classes
System.enqueueJob() must be called before Test.startTest() in a parallel class so the job is queued in time
questions.explain: IsParallel=true comes with restrictions: those tests can't call System.schedule(), System.enqueueJob() or Test.getStandardPricebookId(). This test has to run without IsParallel.
wrong: Queueable jobs don't need org data access.
startTest and stopTest work in parallel tests. The restriction is on enqueueJob.
The job must be enqueued inside the startTest/stopTest block so it runs at stopTest.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: IsTest Annotation

questions.q: A nightly batch class recalculates Account health scores. Its test inserts 400 Accounts and fails at Test.stopTest() with an error saying no more than one executeBatch can be called from within a test method. Which two changes fix the error? (Choose 2)
options: Call Test.stopTest() a second time to run the second chunk
Annotate the test with @IsTest(SeeAllData=true)
Insert 200 or fewer Accounts (and adjust the assertion) so the default scope needs one execute() call
Move Database.executeBatch() above Test.startTest()
Pass a scope that covers all records: Database.executeBatch(new HealthScoreBatch(), 400)
questions.explain: A test can run only one execution of execute(). With the default scope of 200, 400 records need two chunks. Keep the data within one chunk, or raise the scope so every record fits into one execute() call.
wrong: stopTest can be called only once per test method.
Org data access doesn't change how many execute() calls a test allows.
Outside the startTest/stopTest block, the batch doesn't finish before the assertion runs.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using Batch Apex

questions.q: A trigger on Order_Event__e creates a Shipment__c and publishes a Shipment_Event__e. A second trigger, on Shipment_Event__e, inserts a Notification__c. The test below finds the Shipment__c but no Notification__c. What should the developer add?
options: Replace EventBus.publish with Database.insert, because tests can't publish platform events
Annotate the test with SeeAllData=true so the second trigger is subscribed
Call Test.getEventBus().deliver() again before the Notification__c assertion
Call Test.stopTest() a second time right after the first deliver()
questions.explain: Each deliver() call delivers the event messages on the test event bus at that moment. The Shipment_Event__e published by the first trigger needs its own deliver() call before the second subscriber runs.
wrong: EventBus.publish is the supported way to publish events in tests.
Platform event triggers are subscribed in tests without org data access.
stopTest can be called only once per test method.
questions.source: Platform Events Developer Guide: Deliver Test Event Messages

questions.q: A batch class implements Database.RaisesPlatformEvents, and a BatchApexErrorEvent trigger writes failures to Error_Log__c. The test forces a failure in execute(), but it fails at Test.stopTest() and never reaches the assertion. Which two changes make the test work as intended? (Choose 2)
options: Wrap the startTest/executeBatch/stopTest block in try/catch, because the batch exception is passed to the test method
Annotate the test with @IsTest(SeeAllData=true) so BatchApexErrorEvent triggers run
Call Test.getEventBus().deliver() before Database.executeBatch()
After that block, call Test.getEventBus().deliver() to deliver the BatchApexErrorEvent, then assert
Replace Test.stopTest() with Test.getEventBus().deliver(), which also runs the queued batch and its error event
questions.explain: Exceptions in a batch job started by a test are passed to the test method, so catch them around the block. The BatchApexErrorEvent is still waiting on the test event bus, so call Test.getEventBus().deliver() before asserting on the log.
wrong: Event triggers don't need org data access.
Nothing has been published at that point. The event is published when the batch fails.
deliver() delivers event messages. It doesn't run queued batch jobs.
questions.source: Platform Events Developer Guide: Deliver Test Event Messages

questions.q: A developer logs governor usage in a test while investigating a limit problem. The test runs synchronously. What are the values of a and b?
questions.explain: Code between startTest and stopTest gets a fresh set of governor limits, so a counts only the Contact query. After stopTest, the limits that were in effect before startTest apply again, so b is 3.
wrong: startTest starts a new set of limits, so the first 3 queries don't count in a.
After stopTest the original limits come back. The query inside the block isn't added to them.
The Contact query ran after startTest, so a is 1.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Test Class (startTest, stopTest)

questions.q: A test builds a support agent User but the developer forgot to insert it before calling System.runAs. What happens when the test runs?
options: System.runAs throws an exception because the User has no Id
The block runs as the original test user, because runAs ignores users that aren't inserted
It doesn't compile, because runAs only accepts a User Id
runAs inserts the User implicitly, and the code in the block runs as that new user
questions.explain: System.runAs implicitly inserts a User that has been instantiated but not yet inserted, then runs the block as that user. runAs also ignores user license limits.
wrong: runAs handles the new User by inserting it.
The block runs as the User passed in, not as the original user.
runAs takes a User sObject (or a package Version), not an Id.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: System Class (runAs)

questions.q: A territory test (API version 60.0) must create a sales rep User and Accounts in the same test method. Which two approaches avoid a MIXED_DML_OPERATION error? (Choose 2)
options: Insert the User with UserRoleId left null, then insert an Account owned by that User
Insert the User with a UserRoleId, then insert the Account, with both statements directly in the test method
Insert the Account first, then insert the User with a UserRoleId inside System.runAs(new User(Id = UserInfo.getUserId()))
Update an Account, then update a User's ProfileId, both directly in the test method
Insert the User with a UserRoleId and the Account in one call to Database.insert(records, false)
questions.explain: Since API 15.0, a User whose UserRoleId is null can be inserted in the same transaction as other sObjects. When a role is needed, doing the setup DML inside a System.runAs block keeps it apart from the non-setup DML.
wrong: A User with a role plus an Account in one transaction is mixed DML.
Changing ProfileId on a User together with non-setup DML is mixed DML.
Partial success doesn't lift the mixed DML restriction.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: sObjects That Can't Be Used Together in DML Operations

questions.q: A reviewer says this test can never fail, because catch (Exception e) will swallow the failure thrown by Assert.fail(). What actually happens if OrderService.submit(null) does NOT throw?
options: The test passes, because the catch block catches the AssertException
The test fails at Assert.fail(), because a failed assertion can't be caught by a catch block
The test fails inside the catch block, because isInstanceOfType rejects the caught AssertException
It doesn't compile, because Assert.fail() can't appear inside a try block
questions.explain: Exceptions from failed assertions are among the exceptions Apex can't catch, like LimitException. The catch block doesn't run and the test fails with the Assert.fail() message.
wrong: Failed assertions can't be caught, so the catch block never runs.
The catch block never runs for a failed assertion.
Assert.fail() is valid anywhere in a method.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Exception Statements

questions.q: A permission test checks that each of 160 users, spread over several profiles, can update Accounts. The users are inserted with one DML statement before the loop. The test fails with System.LimitException: Too many DML statements: 151. Why?
options: Each call to System.runAs counts against the DML statement limit
runAs inserts each User again, and every insert counts as a DML statement
Describe calls such as isUpdateable() count as DML statements
System.runAs can't be used inside a loop; it must wrap the whole loop
questions.explain: Every call to runAs counts against the total number of DML statements. Two inserts plus 149 runAs calls reach the limit of 150, so the next call fails. Test fewer users per method or split them across test methods.
wrong: runAs only inserts a User that isn't inserted yet. These were already inserted.
Describe calls don't count as DML.
runAs works inside loops. The problem is the DML count.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the runAs Method

questions.q: A shipping integration calls a rates endpoint and then a labels endpoint inside ShippingService.buyLabel(). The team stores a sample response for each endpoint in its own static resource. The test below fails because buyLabel() returns null: the labels call can't parse the response it gets. Which change fixes the test?
options: Put both JSON bodies in the RatesResponse static resource
Register a second StaticResourceCalloutMock with the LabelResponse resource right before calling buyLabel()
Use MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock, map each endpoint to its resource, and register it with Test.setMock
Replace setStaticResource with setBody on the mock, because static resources can't be read from test methods
questions.explain: StaticResourceCalloutMock returns the same response body for every callout, so the labels call gets the rates JSON. MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock returns the static resource mapped to each endpoint.
wrong: The mock still returns one body for both calls, so neither call gets the response it expects.
Both callouts happen inside buyLabel(), so a single-resource mock still returns one body to both calls.
Static resources are readable in tests. That is how these mocks work.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts Using Static Resources

questions.q: A developer writes one reusable mock so a test can fake several endpoints. The class fails to save. What is wrong?
options: respond() must take exactly one HttpRequest parameter. Read the path from req.getEndpoint() instead
A mock class can't be annotated @IsTest
Mock classes can't have constructors that take parameters
respond() must be declared global, so the mock class itself must be global rather than public to save
questions.explain: The interface has a single method, HttpResponse respond(HttpRequest req). With an extra parameter, the interface method isn't implemented. The endpoint is available from req.getEndpoint().
wrong: Mock classes are often annotated @IsTest so they don't count toward the code size limit.
A constructor with parameters is fine. The test passes the values when it creates the mock.
The class that implements HttpCalloutMock can be public or global.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts by Implementing the HttpCalloutMock Interface

questions.q: A developer is mocking a SOAP service whose client classes were generated with WSDL2Apex. Which two statements about the WebServiceMock implementation are correct? (Choose 2)
options: doInvoke returns the generated response element, which the runtime passes to the client
doInvoke puts the generated response element into the response map under the key 'response_x'
The mock is registered with Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new MySoapMock())
The mock class must implement both WebServiceMock and HttpCalloutMock, because SOAP calls are sent over HTTP
The mock class can be public and annotated @IsTest so it doesn't count toward the code size limit
questions.explain: doInvoke returns nothing: it adds the response element to the response map under 'response_x'. The class can be public or global, and @IsTest keeps it out of the 6 MB code size limit. It is registered with Test.setMock(WebServiceMock.class, ...).
wrong: doInvoke is void. The response goes into the response map.
SOAP mocks are registered with WebServiceMock.class.
WebServiceMock alone covers WSDL2Apex callouts.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Test Web Service Callouts

questions.q: A Queueable that implements Database.AllowsCallouts sends invoices to an ERP system. Its test fails with an error saying test methods don't support callouts. What is the fix?
options: Move the insert after Test.startTest(), so uncommitted work doesn't block the callout when the job runs
Add Database.AllowsCallouts to the test class as well, so its test methods are allowed to make callouts
Call Test.setMock inside the Queueable's execute() method
Call Test.setMock before Test.stopTest(), ideally before enqueuing, because the job runs at stopTest
questions.explain: The queued job runs synchronously at Test.stopTest(). The mock is registered only after that, so the callout runs with no mock. Register it before stopTest.
wrong: DML before startTest is the recommended order. It isn't the cause here.
AllowsCallouts is a marker for async classes, not for test classes.
Test setup doesn't belong in production code. The test registers the mock.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Queueable Apex; Testing HTTP Callouts by Implementing the HttpCalloutMock Interface

questions.q: An architect plans to replace slow dependencies with Test.createStub() across a service layer. Which two of these classes can NOT be stubbed with the Stub API? (Choose 2)
options: AccountCleanupBatch, which implements Database.Batchable<SObject>
PricingService, a public top-level class with a public no-argument constructor
TaxCalculator, a public virtual class whose methods return Map<String, Object>
RegistryService, a top-level class whose only constructor is private
ShippingClient, a public top-level class in the same namespace as the test
questions.explain: The Stub API can't mock classes that implement Batchable or classes that have only private constructors. It also can't mock static or private methods, properties, triggers, inner classes or system types.
wrong: A public top-level class with an accessible constructor can be stubbed.
Map return types are fine. Only iterators can't be used as return or parameter types.
A top-level class in the same namespace as the createStub call can be stubbed.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: CatalogService has two overloads, Decimal getPrice(String) and Decimal getPrice(String, Integer), plus Boolean isActive(String). Given the stub provider and test code below, what are a, b and c?
options: a = 10, b = 30, c = true
a = 1.5, b = 1.5, c = false
a = 1.5, b = 30, c = null
a = null, b = 30, c = null
questions.explain: Every call on the stub goes to handleMethodCall. The two-argument overload matches the first branch (10 × 3 = 30), the one-argument overload falls to the Decimal return-type branch (1.5), and isActive gets null.
wrong: The real methods never run, and nothing in the provider returns true.
The two-argument call matches the first branch first, and a null return isn't turned into false.
The one-argument call matches the Decimal return-type branch.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: An ISV team writes its tests in its own namespace, acme. They want Test.createStub() to stub a service class from a partner's managed package (namespace ptnr), and they keep their StubProvider in a shared utility package with a third namespace. What is true?
options: It works, as long as the partner's class is global and virtual
It fails: the stubbed class must be in the test's namespace; the StubProvider can be in any namespace
It fails: the StubProvider must be in the same namespace as the stubbed class; the test can be anywhere
It works only if the test is annotated @IsTest(SeeAllData=true)
questions.explain: The Stub API requires the mocked object to be in the same namespace as the Test.createStub() call. The StubProvider implementation can live in another namespace.
wrong: Being global doesn't lift the namespace rule.
It's the other way around: the stubbed class must match the test's namespace, and the provider can be anywhere.
Data access has nothing to do with stubbing.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: A productCard component uses @wire(getRecord). The Jest test below fails because the .name element is empty. What is the most likely fix?
options: Append the element to the DOM before calling getRecord.emit(); wire data only reaches a connected component
Replace await Promise.resolve() with jest.runAllTimers()
Register the adapter with registerLdsTestWireAdapter(getRecord) before emitting, so emit() reaches the component
Query document.querySelector('.name') instead of using the shadowRoot
questions.explain: A component receives data from the wire service only after it is connected to the DOM. Emitting before appendChild sends the data to no one. Append first, emit, then await a promise before checking the DOM.
wrong: The re-render is a microtask, not a timer, so awaiting a resolved promise is correct.
Registering adapters isn't needed in current sfdx-lwc-jest, and it doesn't fix this: the element must be connected before emit().
Elements inside the component are only reachable through element.shadowRoot.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Write Jest Tests for Lightning Web Components That Use the Wire Service

questions.q: In contactTile, clicking the link runs this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('select', { detail: this.contact.Id })). The test below fails because the handler is never called. What should change?
options: Make the test async and await Promise.resolve() before clicking
Dispatch the event with bubbles: true and composed: true so the test can receive it
Use dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click')) instead of click()
Listen for 'select', not 'onselect'. The on prefix is only used for handlers in a parent's template
questions.explain: addEventListener needs the event name exactly as it was dispatched: 'select'. The onselect form is only for declaring a handler in a parent component's HTML.
wrong: The listener name never matches, so waiting doesn't help.
The test listens on the component's host element, which receives the event without bubbling.
click() already fires a click event on the link.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Create and Dispatch Events; Test Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A Jest test for a refresh button throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'click'). The component template contains <lightning-button label="Refresh" onclick={handleRefresh}>. What is wrong?
options: Base components like lightning-button aren't rendered in Jest, so the test must click a native button instead
The button is in the component's shadow tree, so find it with element.shadowRoot.querySelector()
The test must await a promise before appendChild() so the template renders
document.querySelector only works after jest.useFakeTimers() is called
questions.explain: Elements a component renders live in its shadow tree, which document-level queries can't see. Query through element.shadowRoot.
wrong: sfdx-lwc-jest supplies stubs for base components, so lightning-button is in the shadow tree and can be clicked.
The first render happens when the element is appended. Nothing needs to be awaited before appendChild.
Timers have nothing to do with DOM queries.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: DOM Inspection Tests Are Subject to Change; Test Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A component uses @wire(getContactList), imported from '@salesforce/apex/ContactController.getContactList'. The test below throws TypeError: getContactList.emit is not a function. What should the jest.mock factory return?
options: { default: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue(mockContacts) }
Keep the factory as it is and call getContactList.mockResolvedValue(mockContacts) in the test instead of emit()
{ default: createApexTestWireAdapter(jest.fn()) }, with the helper required from '@salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest'
{ emit: jest.fn() }, so the test can spy on emit
questions.explain: A plain jest.fn() suits imperative Apex calls. When the Apex method is used with @wire, the module's default export must be an Apex test wire adapter, which provides emit() and error().
wrong: A resolved promise is for imperative calls, and the mock still has no emit().
The component never calls a wired method as a promise, so a resolved value doesn't reach the wired property.
The component imports the default export, so the default export itself must be the wire adapter.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Write Jest Tests for Lightning Web Components That Use the Wire Service (lwc-recipes apexWireMethodToProperty test)

questions.q: A developer must prove that accountHeader passes its recordId and the right fields to getRecord, without checking the DOM. NAME_FIELD is imported from @salesforce/schema in both files. Which assertion does this?
options: expect(getRecord.getLastConfig()).toEqual({ recordId: '001xx000003DGb2AAG', fields: [NAME_FIELD] })
expect(getRecord).toHaveBeenCalledWith('001xx000003DGb2AAG')
expect(element.account.data.id).toBe('001xx000003DGb2AAG')
expect(getRecord.emit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ recordId: '001xx000003DGb2AAG' })
questions.explain: Test wire adapters record the configuration the component sends. getLastConfig() returns the latest config, with '$recordId' already replaced by the real value.
wrong: The component doesn't call the adapter like a function, so call assertions don't apply.
account isn't a public property, so the test can't read it from the element, and no data was emitted.
emit() is what the test calls to push data. It doesn't record the config.
questions.source: sfdx-lwc-jest test wire adapters (lwc-recipes apexWireMethodWithParams test)

questions.q: A Visualforce controller extension catches a DmlException in save() and calls ApexPages.addMessages(e). The test below forces the failure. Which assertion best proves that the user would see an error on the page?
options: Assert.isNull(next), because a null PageReference always means an error message was shown
Assert.isTrue(ApexPages.hasMessages(ApexPages.Severity.ERROR))
Assert.areEqual(1, [SELECT COUNT() FROM ApexPageMessage__c])
Assert.isTrue(Test.isRunningTest())
questions.explain: Messages added to the page during a test can be checked with ApexPages.hasMessages(severity) or read with ApexPages.getMessages(). That verifies what the page would show.
wrong: A null return just keeps the user on the same page. It doesn't prove a message was added.
Page messages aren't stored as records.
That only proves the code runs in a test.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: ApexPages Class

questions.q: Users report a JavaScript error in a Lightning web component in a sandbox. In the browser's developer tools, the framework and component code is minified and hard to follow. Which two actions help the developer debug the component's JavaScript? (Choose 2)
options: Set the Apex Code log level to FINEST for the user
Enable Debug Mode for the developer's user in Setup so Lightning JavaScript isn't minified
Run the component's Jest tests against the sandbox with --target-org
Open a downloaded debug log in Apex Replay Debugger to step through the component's JavaScript
Add a debugger statement or set a breakpoint in the browser's Sources panel, then reproduce the issue
questions.explain: Debug Mode serves Lightning JavaScript unminified, which makes browser debugging practical. Breakpoints or a debugger statement then pause the code in the browser's developer tools.
wrong: Debug logs cover server-side code, not JavaScript in the browser.
Jest tests run locally in Node.js and never connect to an org.
Replay Debugger replays Apex from debug logs, not browser JavaScript.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Debug Lightning Web Components; Salesforce Help: Enable Debug Mode for Lightning Components

questions.q: An import utility logs its failures to a custom object. During a large import, users get an error and no Import_Log__c record is written, and the debug log shows no "Import finished" line. What explains this?
options: The catch block runs, but its insert is rolled back because DML inside a try statement only commits on success
A QueryException is thrown first, and catch (Exception e) can't catch it
The 101st query throws System.LimitException, which can't be caught, so the whole transaction rolls back
The finally block runs first and ends the transaction before catch can log
questions.explain: The query in the loop exceeds the SOQL limit. LimitException can't be caught: catch and finally blocks don't run, and the transaction rolls back. Bulkify the query, or check Limits.getQueries() before reaching the limit.
wrong: For catchable exceptions, catch (Exception e) runs and its DML commits.
QueryException is catchable with catch (Exception e).
finally runs after catch, and it doesn't end the transaction.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Exception Statements

questions.q: A support engineer chasing an intermittent bug leaves FINEST logging on for an integration user that runs all day. Which two statements about debug log limits are correct? (Choose 2)
options: A log larger than 20 MB is reduced by removing older log lines, which can come from anywhere in the log
A log larger than 20 MB is discarded completely and replaced by a single entry saying the log was too large
While the Developer Console is open, debug logs are generated for every user in the org
If more than 1,000 MB of debug logs is generated in 15 minutes, trace flags are disabled
System debug logs are kept for 30 days
questions.explain: Logs over 20 MB are trimmed by removing older lines, and generating more than 1,000 MB of logs in a 15-minute window disables trace flags. System debug logs are kept for 24 hours.
wrong: The log is trimmed, not discarded.
The Developer Console records logs for its own user only.
System debug logs are kept for 24 hours; monitoring debug logs for seven days.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Debug Log

questions.q: An integration user calls OrderService through a REST endpoint. To get detail from that class only, a developer adds an Apex class trace flag on OrderService with Apex Code set to FINEST, then waits. No debug logs appear for the integration calls. What should the developer do?
options: Add System = FINEST to the class trace flag's debug level
Add a trigger trace flag on every trigger that OrderService fires
Keep the Developer Console open while the calls run, because it records logs for every user while it's open
Add a user trace flag for the integration user; class trace flags don't start logging on their own
questions.explain: Class and trigger trace flags override log levels for that code but don't cause logs to be generated. A user trace flag on the integration user turns logging on, and the class flag then sets the detail for OrderService.
wrong: More categories on the class flag still don't start logging.
Trigger trace flags don't generate logs on their own either.
The Developer Console captures logs for its own user, not other users.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Debug Log

questions.q: After a release, updating 120 Opportunities with Data Loader fails. The developer pulls this excerpt from the debug log. What is the root cause?
questions.code:
13:02:11.204 (204511000)|CODE_UNIT_STARTED|[EXTERNAL]|01qxx0000004C9z|OpportunityTrigger on Opportunity trigger event AfterUpdate
13:02:11.209 (209881000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_BEGIN|[14]|Aggregations:0|SELECT Id, Rating FROM Account WHERE Id = :tmpVar1
13:02:11.212 (212004000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_END|[14]|Rows:1
13:02:11.215 (215120000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_BEGIN|[14]|Aggregations:0|SELECT Id, Rating FROM Account WHERE Id = :tmpVar1
13:02:11.217 (217337000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_END|[14]|Rows:1
... the same pair repeats, always at line [14] ...
13:02:11.871 (871220000)|EXCEPTION_THROWN|[14]|System.LimitException: Too many SOQL queries: 101
13:02:11.871 (871390000)|FATAL_ERROR|System.LimitException: Too many SOQL queries: 101
options: Data Loader sends 1,000 records per trigger call, which lowers the query limit
Line 14 runs an Account query per Opportunity inside a loop. Query once with a set of Ids before it
The Account query isn't selective, so it times out and is retried automatically until the SOQL limit is hit
The trigger should catch the LimitException and retry the remaining records in a Queueable
questions.explain: Every SOQL_EXECUTE_BEGIN comes from the same line [14], with one bind value and one row each time: the pattern of a query inside a loop. One query with WHERE Id IN :accountIds before the loop fixes it.
wrong: Triggers process records in chunks of up to 200. The limit is the same; the per-record query is the problem.
Each query returns one row within milliseconds. It isn't a timeout.
LimitException can't be caught.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Debug Log; Execution Governors and Limits

questions.q: A nightly batch job should create a follow-up Task for each Opportunity. The job completes, no exception appears in the debug log, but many Tasks are missing. What is the most likely cause?
options: With allOrNone false, failed records are returned in SaveResults instead of throwing, and nobody checks them
Tasks inserted in execute() are held until finish() runs, and they're dropped if finish() doesn't commit them
DML in execute() is deferred to the next execute() call, so records from the last chunk are never saved
WhatId can't be set from Apex, so those Tasks are skipped
questions.explain: With allOrNone = false, records that fail (for example because the owner is an inactive user) don't throw. The errors are only in the returned Database.SaveResult list, so the code should check isSuccess() and log getErrors().
wrong: Records inserted in execute() are committed when that execute() transaction ends.
DML isn't deferred between execute() calls.
WhatId can be set on Task from Apex.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Database Class; SaveResult Class

questions.q: A CI script builds an unlocked package version. The pipeline owner wants fast builds, but the version must be promotable to released. The command below fails right away. Why?
questions.code:
sf package version create \
  --package "Billing Core" \
  --installation-key-bypass \
  --skip-validation \
  --code-coverage \
  --wait 30
options: --installation-key-bypass can't be used with unlocked packages, so the version needs an --installation-key
--skip-validation can't be combined with --code-coverage, and skip-validation versions can't be promoted
--wait must be at least 60 minutes when --code-coverage is set
Unlocked packages compute coverage at promote time, so --code-coverage isn't a valid flag
questions.explain: Code coverage is calculated as part of validation, so skipping validation and computing coverage are mutually exclusive. Versions created with skip validation can't be promoted, so a promotable build needs validation plus --code-coverage.
wrong: Installation key bypass is valid for unlocked packages.
There is no such minimum wait time.
Coverage is computed with --code-coverage at version creation, and promotion requires it.
questions.source: Salesforce DX Developer Guide: Create New Versions of an Unlocked Package; Code Coverage for Unlocked Packages

questions.q: A release manager is planning environments for a regulated insurer. Which two statements about sandboxes are correct? (Choose 2)
options: A Developer sandbox includes a sample of production data chosen by a sandbox template
A Partial Copy sandbox copies all production data but no metadata
A Developer Pro sandbox can be refreshed once a day
Refreshing a sandbox keeps the sandbox's own changes and adds production's new metadata
A Full sandbox can be refreshed every 29 days
questions.explain: Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes have a one-day refresh interval, and Full sandboxes 29 days. Only Partial Copy (a template-selected sample) and Full sandboxes copy production data.
wrong: Developer sandboxes copy metadata only. Templates are for Partial Copy and Full sandboxes.
Partial Copy copies all metadata plus a sample of data chosen by a template.
A refresh replaces the sandbox with a new copy of production, so its own changes are lost.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Sandbox Types and Templates

questions.q: A release pipeline must read per-class coverage after tests run in a sandbox, to block merges below 85%. The command below fails with sObject type 'ApexCodeCoverageAggregate' is not supported. What is the fix?
questions.code:
sf data query \
  --query "SELECT ApexClassOrTrigger.Name, NumLinesCovered, NumLinesUncovered FROM ApexCodeCoverageAggregate" \
  --target-org uat
options: Add --use-tooling-api, because ApexCodeCoverageAggregate is a Tooling API object
Retrieve ApexCodeCoverageAggregate with sf project retrieve start, because it is Metadata API metadata
Run the query in Execute Anonymous, because coverage records are only visible from Apex
Query a coverage field on ApexClass through the standard API instead
questions.explain: Coverage records such as ApexCodeCoverageAggregate are Tooling API objects. sf data query needs --use-tooling-api to query Tooling API objects.
wrong: Coverage results aren't metadata components, so they can't be retrieved.
Apex SOQL can't query Tooling API objects.
ApexClass has no coverage field. Coverage lives in Tooling API objects.
questions.source: Tooling API Developer Guide: ApexCodeCoverageAggregate; Salesforce CLI Command Reference: data query

questions.q: A team that relies heavily on admins is moving from change sets to DevOps Center. Which statement describes how DevOps Center manages changes?
options: It packages each work item into an outbound change set and uploads it to the next connected org in the pipeline
It requires every developer to work in scratch orgs created from a Dev Hub
Work items are committed to a source control repository and promoted through pipeline stages
It lets work items skip Apex tests when they are promoted to production
questions.explain: DevOps Center is built on source control. The changes for each work item are committed to a repository and promoted through the stages of a pipeline, instead of being moved with change sets.
wrong: DevOps Center replaces change sets with promotion based on source control.
Development environments can be sandboxes. Scratch orgs aren't required.
Deployments to production still follow the normal Apex test requirements.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: DevOps Center

questions.q: Before a release, a developer wants to check that the changes deploy cleanly to the UAT sandbox, including running local tests, without changing UAT. The team lead says the command below is the wrong tool for a sandbox. Which command should the developer use?
questions.code: sf project deploy validate --source-dir force-app --target-org uat
options: sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --target-org uat --test-level RunLocalTests --ignore-conflicts
sf project deploy quick --source-dir force-app --target-org uat
sf project deploy preview --source-dir force-app --target-org uat
sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --target-org uat --dry-run --test-level RunLocalTests
questions.explain: deploy validate is meant for production orgs. For a sandbox, the CLI reference recommends deploy start with --dry-run and an explicit test level: it validates and runs the tests without saving anything.
wrong: Without --dry-run this really deploys to UAT and changes it.
quick deploys an earlier validation by job ID. It doesn't validate source.
preview only lists what would deploy and possible conflicts. It runs no tests.
questions.source: Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project deploy validate

questions.q: A validation against production succeeded on Monday morning. On Saturday the release manager runs the command below, and it reports that no validated deployment was found. Nothing else has been validated since Monday. What should they do?
questions.code: sf project deploy quick --use-most-recent --target-org prod
options: Validate again, because a validated job ID expires after 3 days
Pass the job ID with --job-id. It stays valid for 10 days, but --use-most-recent only looks back 3 days
Add --test-level RunLocalTests so quick deploy can run the tests again
Run sf project deploy resume --use-most-recent, which turns the most recent validation into a deployment
questions.explain: --use-most-recent only finds validations from the past 3 days. The job ID itself is valid for 10 days from the start of the validation, so passing it with --job-id works.
wrong: The job ID is valid for 10 days. Only the --use-most-recent lookup is limited to 3 days.
Quick deploy skips tests because they already ran during validation.
resume watches an operation that is still running. It doesn't deploy a validation.
questions.source: Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project deploy quick

questions.q: The custom field Account.Legacy_Code__c is referenced by the Apex class AccountMapper. The team wants one deployment that updates AccountMapper to remove the reference and also deletes the field. In which manifest should the field be listed?
questions.code:
<!-- package.xml -->
<Package xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
  <types>
    <members>AccountMapper</members>
    <name>ApexClass</name>
  </types>
  <version>62.0</version>
</Package>

<!-- deletion manifest: which file? -->
<Package xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
  <types>
    <members>Account.Legacy_Code__c</members>
    <name>CustomField</name>
  </types>
</Package>
options: destructiveChangesPre.xml, so the field is deleted before the class is compiled
package.xml, with a delete flag on the members element
destructiveChangesPost.xml, so the field is deleted after AccountMapper is updated
destructiveChanges.xml with <members>*</members> to remove every unused field
questions.explain: Post-destructive changes run after the other components are deployed, so AccountMapper drops its reference first and the field can then be deleted. Post-destructive changes are processed before tests run.
wrong: Deleting first fails, because the current AccountMapper still references the field.
package.xml has no delete option. Deletions go in a destructive changes manifest.
Wildcards aren't supported in destructive changes manifests, and plain destructiveChanges.xml deletes before additions.
questions.source: Metadata API Developer Guide: Deleting Components from an Organization

questions.q: A team is writing CI rules for sf project deploy start. Which two statements about test levels are correct? (Choose 2)
options: RunAllTestsInOrg skips tests that come from installed managed packages
NoTestRun applies only to development environments such as sandboxes, Developer Edition and trial orgs
With RunSpecifiedTests, the deployment passes as long as org-wide coverage stays at 75%, whatever each class reaches
RunLocalTests runs every test in the org except tests from installed managed and unlocked packages
sf project deploy validate defaults to NoTestRun unless --test-level is set
questions.explain: NoTestRun is only for development environments, and RunLocalTests leaves out tests from installed managed and unlocked packages. RunSpecifiedTests needs 75% coverage for each class and trigger, and deploy validate defaults to RunLocalTests.
wrong: RunAllTestsInOrg includes managed package tests.
RunSpecifiedTests requires 75% coverage for each class and trigger in the deployment.
deploy validate requires tests and defaults to RunLocalTests.
questions.source: Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project deploy start; project deploy validate
